title: The Evening Brief: Crises converge: Germany's far-right surges as disasters compound across continents
dek: Exit polls confirmed Germany's AfD winning 44 percent in Saxony-Anhalt while rescue operations continued in Delhi, Hurricane Lowell approached Hawaii, and multiple crises tested response capacity across three continents.
author: GoCheckMyNews
key_fact: Monday compressed multiple emergencies into a single news cycle: Germany's far-right achieved its strongest postwar result before any governing path emerged; rescue work in Delhi raced against time as basement debris remained to be cleared; Hurricane Lowell approached Hawaii with impacts due Monday night; and simultaneous military escalation in the Strait of Hormuz sent oil prices to six-week highs, driving U.S. fuel costs up 7 cents in a week.
bottom_line: Monday compressed political upheaval, natural disaster response, military escalation, and economic pressure into a single news cycle where outcomes remained fluid. Germany's far-right achieved an unprecedented result before any coalition path clarified; Delhi's rescue operation raced against time with basement debris still to be cleared; Hurricane Lowell approached Hawaii with impacts due Monday night; and oil prices jumped on military strikes in the Strait of Hormuz, driving U.S. fuel costs to record holiday levels. Watch for Germany's final vote tallies and coalition negotiations, Delhi casualty confirmations as rescue work concludes, Lowell's actual track in the 36 hours before Tuesday morning, and whether oil prices stabilize or reflect sustained supply disruption.
body: Monday's news cycle pivoted on compressed timeframes where outcomes remained uncertain even as events unfolded. Germany's exit polls confirmed the AfD at 44 percent in Saxony-Anhalt, the strongest far-right result in any German state since World War II, but the party fell short of the 50 percent needed to govern alone, leaving coalition negotiations unclear. Germany's mainstream parties have long refused to work with the AfD, creating a potential political impasse in a 2.1 million-person state. Final vote tallies will clarify whether a path to government exists.

In Delhi, rescue operations continued at the collapsed Hostel Daze, where at least seven people were killed and 12 hospitalized after a five-storey student residence caved in on September 6 around 13:30 local time. As of Monday morning, roughly 80 percent of debris had been cleared, but basement rubble remained to be searched. The exact number of people trapped or missing stayed unclear; eyewitnesses had cited two to four dozen occupants. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta attributed the collapse to water accumulation and ongoing basement repair work, though authorities said the precise cause remained under investigation. The building owner was arrested and five senior civic officials suspended.

Hurricane Lowell remained on approach to Hawaii as a Category 3 storm with sustained winds of 120-125 mph, positioned roughly 545 miles south-southwest of Lihue as of September 7. Governor Josh Green declared a state of emergency and activated the National Guard on September 6, with first impacts expected by Monday evening, September 9. Forecasts project the storm will reach Hawaii as a Category 2 hurricane, with its center passing approximately 130 miles west of Niihau or 170 miles west of Kauai between Monday evening and Tuesday morning. Rainfall forecasts range from 6 to 10 inches, with maximum totals up to 14 inches possible on Kauai and Niihau. A tropical storm warning remained in effect for both islands. Lowell is the third tropical system to threaten Hawaii in just over three weeks; as of September 7, Hurricanes Karina, Lowell, and Marie were churning in the Pacific simultaneously, the region's first triple-hurricane stretch in a decade.

Military escalation in the Strait of Hormuz drove oil prices sharply higher. Brent crude rose to approximately 97 dollars per barrel on Monday, a nine percent increase over five days and a six-week high. U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude similarly reached 92.27 dollars per barrel. The escalation followed reported U.S. strikes on three Iranian oil tankers on Saturday and Iranian Revolutionary Guard claims of strikes on three tankers and U.S.-linked vessels. Shipping through the chokepoint, which carries roughly one-fifth of global oil supply, declined to an average of 10 commodity ships crossing daily over the prior ten days. U.S. gasoline prices climbed 7 cents in a week to an average of 4.15 dollars per gallon on Labor Day, the highest price ever recorded for that holiday, according to AAA. California prices regularly exceeded 6 dollars per gallon. Diesel hit an all-time high of 5.90 dollars per gallon nationally.

Elsewhere, Kyiv endured 76 air raid alerts in the seven days from August 27 to September 2, the highest weekly count since Russia's full-scale invasion began in 2022. Russia has shifted from primarily nighttime attacks to round-the-clock strikes; alerts now sound an average of 10 times per day. Newer jet-engine-powered attack drones fly at nearly 370 mph, three times as fast as older Shahed drones and harder to intercept. A five-day fireworks explosion at a village festival in central Mexico on September 6 killed at least 10 and wounded at least 60; preliminary reports suggest a burning straw bull effigy ignited a larger cache stored in a church. A Boeing 767 cargo aircraft operated by 21 Air overran Runway 30 at Miami International Airport on September 6, killing five and injuring five, with three critically wounded. The plane landed at approximately 185 mph from San Juan, Puerto Rico, overran the runway by 1,300 feet, and struck a service van and civilian vehicle. NTSB investigators are examining whether runway safety infrastructure could have prevented the overflight.

On the political front, an armed man was arrested at the Canfield Fair in Ohio on September 6 after pushing through a crowd near Democratic gubernatorial nominee Amy Acton. Patrick Havas, 38, of Canfield, was found carrying two handguns, a Taser, and brass knuckles but did not brandish them. Ohio State Highway Patrol security confronted him, and two people were knocked to the ground. Havas was arrested on charges of disorderly conduct and two counts of assault. In the Trump administration's third emergency appeal to the Supreme Court on September 6, the Justice Department sought to reinstate a USPS rule restricting mail-in ballots. U.S. District Judge Indira Talwani had blocked the rule on September 5, ruling it would "threaten disenfranchisement of millions" of voters less than seventy days before the November election. North Carolina began mailing ballots, with Alabama set to start on September 9. An NBC News Decision Desk Poll conducted August 20 through September 1 found 69 percent of voters in swing districts oppose AI data center construction locally, cutting across party lines: 57 percent of Republicans, 81 percent of Democrats, and 71 percent of independents opposed. In Britain, Jaguar Land Rover announced 4,000 job cuts over two years, roughly 9 percent of its global workforce, as it attempts to save 1.7 billion pounds amid U.S. tariffs, Chinese competition, and EV transition costs. Sales had slumped by a fifth to 22.9 billion pounds in the prior two-year period. King Charles III issued a formal letter on September 7 confirming Prince Harry and Meghan remain non-working members of the royal family following their return to the U.K. from California, clarifying they cannot use the titles HRH.
